body.p: 1. Introduction
The Applicant has carefully reviewed the rejections raised in the Office Action

mailed on July 16, 2024. As a result, the claims have been amended as outlined below. Claims 1, 41, and 42 have been cancelled, claims 47, 48, 50-52, and 57-59 have been amended, and new claims 65 and 66 have been added. Claims 47-66 remain in the application. Reconsideration of the application, as amended, is requested.
2. Claim Amendments
The Applicant has made amendments to the claims as indicated above, and entry of these amendments is respectfully requested.

In order to expedite prosecution of the present application, claims 1, 41 and 42, which are drawn to unelected Group I, have been cancelled. The Applicant reserves the right to file divisional or continuing applications drawn to these claims.

It is respectfully submitted that all the amendments made herein are supported by the application as originally filed, and that no new matter has been added by the amendments. Support for the amendments can be found in the application as originally filed as follows.

Claim 47 has been amended to limit the positioning element such that it is sized and shaped to be capable of registering with the size and shape of a particular anatomic location on a chest of the patient, such that the positioning element can be repeatedly and stably positionable on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location. This amendment is supported, for example, in the specification in paragraphs [0019] and [0095]. The claim has also been amended to add structure to the recitation of the reference element, recasting the reference element as a reference structure connected to or integrated with the positioning element, having known spatial characteristics, the reference structure being positionable with respect to the neck of the patient by positioning of the locator object, which is supported, for example, in the specification in paragraphs [0013], [0015], [0024]-[0026]. The claim has also been amended to clarify that the processor is configured to determine a jugular venous pressure (JVP) height
based on the known spatial characteristics of the reference structure, as supported, for example, in the specification in paragraphs [0013], [0050], [0092] and [0138].
Claims 48, 51, 52, 57 and 58 have been amended to conform to the amendments made to claim 47.
Claims 50 and 59 have been amended to employ the words "the" to refer to the chest and the patient, as per antecedent support for these terms in claim 47.
New claims 65 and 66 are supported, for example, in the specification in paragraphs [0026], [0032] and [0088].
3. Claim Rejections - 35 USC Section 112

On pages 2 and 3 of the Office Action, the Examiner has rejected claims 47-64 under 35 USC Section 112, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the Applicant regards as the invention.
Regarding claim 47, the Examiner objects to a lack of clarity pertaining to the

specific nature of the reference element. As noted above, claim 47 has been amended to clarify that the reference element is a physical structure that is connected to or integrated with the positioning element, thereby addressing the present rejection.
Claim 47 has also been amended to correct the antecedent issue with the first

instance of the phrase "the patient", with the claim now referring to "a patient". Likewise, claim 50 has been amended to refer to "the patient" instead of "a patient", and claim 59 has been amended to refer to "the neck of the patient", replacing the phrase "a neck of a patient".
In view of the present amendments, the Applicant kindly requests the withdrawal of the 112 rejections.
4. Claim Rejections - 35 USC Section 102(b)

On pages 4-6 of the Office Action, the Examiner has rejected claims 47-48, 51- 52, 57-58, and 62-64 under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by DeBusschere (US 20170296119 AI). The Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections on the basis that DeBusschere fails to disclose each and every limitation of claim 47, as presently amended.

Claim 47, as presently amended, requires that the imaging assembly is coupled to and spaced from the positioning structure such that the imaging assembly is configured to capture imaging data of at least a portion of a neck of the patient and at least a portion of the reference structure. The reference structure is a physical structure that is connected to, or integrated with, the positioning element, and is positioned to be imaged, at least in part, by the imaging assembly.
In stark contrast, the reference element identified in DeBusschere by the

Examiner is a virtual annotation that is digitally overlaid on an image acquired by the camera of DeBusschere. For example, in paragraph [0032], DeBusschere describes the line 118 (presented on the display of the device shown in FIG. 1) as being an "indication overlaying the reconstructed video". DeBusschere therefore differs from the claimed invention in two significant ways:
(i) DeBusschere, in only showing a virtual annotation on an image, fails to
disclose or teach the claimed reference structure that is connected to or
integrated with the positioning element and thus is a real physical
structure, and
(ii) DeBusschere, in only showing a virtual annotation on an image, fails to
disclose or teach the claimed configuration in which the imaging assembly is configured to capture imaging data of at least a portion of a neck of the
patient and at least a portion of the reference structure.

In absence of the disclosure by DeBusschere of either of these aspects of claim 47, one concludes that claim 47 is novel and non-obvious in view of the limited disclosure and teachings of DeBusschere.

Moreover the Applicant takes the opportunity to identify another novel and non- obvious aspect of the claimed invention relative to the limited disclosure and teachings of DeBusschere. While the Examiner infers DeBusschere's use of a band that wraps around the patient as disclosing the claimed positioning element, the band of DeBusschere can be moved up and down, and can also be rotated, relative to the body of the patient, and as a consequence of these spatial degrees of freedom, it is clear that

DeBusschere fails to disclose the claimed positioning element that is sized and shaped to be capable of registering with the size and shape of a particular anatomic location on a chest of the patient. Accordingly, DeBusschere fails to disclose or teach the claimed spatial registration between the positioning element and the anatomical location. The absence of this spatial registration prevents the DeBusschere device from being repeatedly and stably positionable on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location, thereby failing to ensure that at least a portion of the reference structure is positioned, relative to the body, such that the image data captured by the imaging assembly includes at least a portion of the reference structure.

Accordingly, in the absence of the disclosure and teaching by DeBusschere of the aforementioned aspects of the invention recited in claim 47, it is respectfully submitted that claim 47, and all claims dependent therefrom, is novel and non-obvious.
5. Claim Rejections - 35 USC Section 103(a)

On pages 6-9 of the Office Action, the Examiner has rejected claims 49, 50, 59, and 61 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over DeBusschere in view of Rogers (US 20210113099 AI). On pages 9 and 10 of the Office Action, the Examiner has also rejected claims 53-56 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over DeBusschere in view of Tzvieli (US 20200221956 AI). Furthermore, on pages 10 and 11 of the Office Action, the Examiner has rejected claim 60 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over DeBusschere in view of Wagle (US 20170027457 AI).

The Applicant points out that these rejections are directed to the dependent claims and are not applied to the limitations of independent claim 67. In view of the comments provided above regarding the patentability of claim 67 over DeBusschere, it is respectfully submitted that claims 49, 50, 53-56, 59, 60 and 61 are non-obvious at least as a result of their respective dependence on claim 47.
6. Conclusions
In view of the foregoing, the Applicant respectfully requests favorable
consideration and allowance of the claims. Should the Examiner have any questions regarding this response or the allowability of the claims, the Applicant would appreciate

if the Examiner would contact the undersigned attorney of record at the telephone number provided below for purposes of facilitating prosecution of this application. Any additional fees necessary to complete this submission only may be charged to Dowell & Dowell, P.C. deposit account no. 04-1577.
Respectfully submitted, Dowell & Dowell, P.C.
